title: Frequency-specific cortical swallowing-network responses following neuroengineering-guided individualized multichannel tDCS.
claim_mapping: Healthy-volunteer neuromodulation feasibility; no patient burden or clinical efficacy endpoint relevant to current claims.
caveat: Eight healthy adults; corrected primary interaction nonsignificant. Do not use exploratory within-group changes as treatment benefit.

title: In-hospital mortality in co-occurring dehydration and dysphagia: results from the nationwide GEMIDAS Pro registry.
claim_mapping: External national evidence linking coded dysphagia and volume depletion to hospital prognosis; supports E86 discussion.
caveat: Geriatric admissions aged 65+ in GEMIDAS 2006–2024, not the InEK OPS cohorts; adjusted ORs not equivalent to current RRs; overlaps same registry as PMID42361766.

title: Frequency-specific cortical subnetworks support fast human swallowing.
claim_mapping: Basic physiology of cortical connectivity during swallowing in healthy adults; beyond hospital-burden focus.
caveat: 74 healthy adults, no dysphagic clinical cohort or service outcome.

title: Reliability and validity of the DEFISS score for predicting post-extubation dysphagia and dysphagia-related reintubation after stroke.
claim_mapping: Clinical severity and airway protection missing from administrative data; risk-stratified assessment in ventilated stroke.
caveat: Prospective n39, only five dysphagia-related reintubations; not broad national external validation and not an InEK severity-adjustment instrument.

title: Dysphagia as a geriatric syndrome: nationwide outcomes from the GEMIDAS registry.
claim_mapping: Independent national geriatric data-source comparison for dysphagia as marker of mortality, aspiration coding and adverse discharge.
caveat: GEMIDAS geriatric admissions, R13 main OR secondary; different case mix and exposure from InEK secondary-only; overlaps PMID42862540.

title: Multifeature endoscopic swallowing patterns associated with pneumonia in hospitalized geriatric patients: a four-year longitudinal cohort study.
claim_mapping: Clinical FEES findings beyond binary aspiration relate to longer-term pneumonia; supports phenotyping rather than judging R13 severity.
caveat: Retrospective n98 geriatric cohort with internal model assessment; likely overlaps same 98-patient four-year cohort as PMID40606509, so not independent replication.

title: Cough reflex testing for dysphagia severity and pneumonia risk after acute stroke: a prospective observational study.
claim_mapping: Airway protection and cough modify the relationship between swallowing dysfunction and respiratory complications.
caveat: Prospective n395 acute-stroke ICU cohort; cough test has imperfect diagnostic accuracy and does not replace FEES or prove a prevention effect.

title: A multidisciplinary Delphi consensus on the formulation of an optimized oral diet for dysphagia and malnutrition (FOOD-DM).
claim_mapping: Relevant only if a detailed nutritional-management recommendation is added; integrates texture and nutrition.
caveat: Expert Delphi framework, not trial evidence that modified diets reduce pneumonia or mortality; current burden manuscripts do not test diet formulations.

title: [Oropharyngeal dysphagia as a neurogeriatric syndrome].
claim_mapping: German neurogeriatric review supports broad syndrome framing but overlaps the fuller English neurogeriatric review already selected.
caveat: Narrative review with B Labeit initials; disambiguated via Düsseldorf affiliation and public institutional email. Avoid redundant review citation.

title: Mapping neurogenic dysphagia diagnostics in Germany: accessibility, implementation practices, and barriers to swallowing endoscopy.
claim_mapping: National German implementation/access context for FEES use and continuity between acute, rehabilitation and outpatient care.
caveat: 82 certified instructors, 52.6% response; self-report and advertised-service mapping, not a census of patient-level inpatient use or proof of guideline nonadherence.

title: Pharyngeal electrical stimulation for postextubation dysphagia after stroke: a randomized trial on hospitalization costs from a health insurance perspective.
claim_mapping: Separates observed LOS/resource burden from proven intervention savings; economic follow-up of PES pilot.
caveat: Secondary economic analysis of SAME n60 trial as PMIDs37789340 and40383663. Mean DRG expenditure difference nonsignificant (one-sided p=.087); no proven cost effectiveness.

title: Impact of a Neurogenic Dysphagia Outpatient Clinic on Diagnosis, Treatment, and Nutrition.
claim_mapping: Care continuity and reassessment after discharge; specialized neurogenic dysphagia service changes diagnosis and management.
caveat: Retrospective selected 255 outpatients; no untreated control and not an early-rehabilitation efficacy trial.

title: Effect of deep brain stimulation on dysphagia in Parkinson's disease: mechanisms, evidence, and outlook.
claim_mapping: Disease-specific Parkinson/DBS therapy review; not needed for current aggregate burden or FEES/PEG/tracheotomy claims.
caveat: Not a stroke or early-rehabilitation intervention study; avoid generalizing DBS evidence.

title: Metaplasticity in swallowing system via cross-modal neurostimulation: A randomized crossover trial with magnetoencephalography.
claim_mapping: Healthy-volunteer cross-modal stimulation physiology, outside clinical burden question.
caveat: 21 healthy volunteers; no significant swallowing-behavior change and no patient outcome evidence.

title: Oropharyngeal dysphagia: a narrative review towards an integrated neurogeriatric perspective.
claim_mapping: Neurogeriatric framework for age, comorbidity and mixed dysphagia mechanisms; supports R13 as a heterogeneous syndrome.
caveat: Narrative review, not a source for numerical prevalence or adjusted outcome estimates.

title: [Challenges and potential of geriatric research in Germany-Insights from the GERisearch survey].
claim_mapping: Survey of geriatric physicians' research working conditions, unrelated to study endpoints.
caveat: Research infrastructure survey is not dysphagia service utilization evidence.

title: Classifying neurogenic dysphagia: neuroanatomical hierarchy versus clinical syndromology.
claim_mapping: Conceptual discussion of dysphagia classification; broader phenotyping is supported better by the validated 2021 classification paper.
caveat: Editorial/comment without abstract; full text not critically appraised, therefore no numerical or novel clinical claim assigned.

title: Gaps in Guidelines on Long-Term Management Strategies for Post-Stroke Dysphagia.
claim_mapping: Evidence gap for structured long-term reassessment and pathways following inpatient rehabilitation.
caveat: Guideline synthesis/position paper, not comparative treatment-effect evidence; does not show that all current care is inadequate.

title: Endoscopic characterization of oropharyngeal dysphagia in patients with dementia.
claim_mapping: Dementia-specific FEES phenotypes illustrate heterogeneity, but dementia-specific analysis is not part of current manuscripts.
caveat: Selected n107 hospitalized geriatric patients; cannot estimate early-rehabilitation prevalence; broader phenotype paper covers current claim.

title: Prognostic value of cough force measured by peak expiratory flow in a 4-year longitudinal cohort study of geriatric patients with oropharyngeal dysphagia.
claim_mapping: Cough force and long-term pulmonary risk support broader airway-safety assessment beyond a diagnosis code.
caveat: n98 geriatric cohort, four-year follow-up, not in-hospital outcome; likely same cohort as PMID42304253.

title: Treating postextubation dysphagia after stroke with pharyngeal electrical stimulation -insights from a randomized controlled pilot trial.
claim_mapping: Detailed dysphagia recovery and hospital-stay secondary outcomes after PES provide intervention-specific context.
caveat: SAME n60 randomized pilot as PMID37789340; secondary trajectories, not a second independent RCT; generalization to all coded dysphagia inappropriate.

title: Subcutaneous Foslevodopa as Novel Rescue Therapy for Akinetic Crisis in Parkinson's Disease: A Case Report.
claim_mapping: Akinetic-crisis rescue therapy case report, not a source for dysphagia burden or care-pathway claims.
caveat: No PubMed abstract; title and publication metadata establish narrow case-report scope.

title: Cognitive decline limits compensatory resource allocation within the aged swallowing network.
claim_mapping: Cognition and swallowing reserve in older volunteers could contextualize missing cognition data, but not needed in focused burden discussion.
caveat: 63 older volunteers without preexisting dysphagia-causing disease; no hospital outcome estimates.

title: Decannulation ahead: a comprehensive diagnostic and therapeutic framework for tracheotomized neurological patients.
claim_mapping: Tracheotomy, secretion management, cough and swallowing assessment as components of decannulation pathways.
caveat: Clinical review/framework; no efficacy estimate and cannot identify inappropriate tracheotomy or delayed decannulation from OPS coding.

title: Associations of inferior frontal sulcal hyperintensities on brain MRI with cerebral small vessel disease, cognitive function, and depression symptoms.
claim_mapping: Brain MRI biomarker associations with cognition/depression; no relevant dysphagia or care outcome question.
caveat: CSVD imaging cohort, unrelated to the present study endpoints.

title: Dietary intervention for post-stroke dysphagia - Authors' reply.
claim_mapping: Author reply associated with the 2024 stroke-treatment review; no independent evidence to add.
caveat: No PubMed abstract; correspondence, not a distinct intervention trial; primary review preferred.

title: New and Evolving Treatments for Neurologic Dysphagia.
claim_mapping: Broader neurogenic dysphagia treatment landscape relevant to the mixed neurological early-rehabilitation cohort.
caveat: Narrative review, not evidence that every patient is eligible for PES or that recorded intervention frequencies measure underuse.

title: Systematic approach to contextualize findings of flexible endoscopic evaluation of swallowing in neurogenic dysphagia- towards an integrated FEES report.
claim_mapping: FEES reports should integrate phenotype, severity, etiology and management; explains information absent from the OPS 1-613 flag.
caveat: Clinical reporting framework/review, not an outcome trial or a validated administrative severity measure.

title: Which Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA) instruments are currently used in Germany: a survey.
claim_mapping: German geriatric assessment practice survey is adjacent service evidence, but more specific FEES access study better fits current claims.
caveat: 76 analyzed survey records; not a neurorehabilitation service census or dysphagia outcome study.

title: Pharyngeal Electrical Stimulation prior to extubation - Reduction of extubation failure rate in acute stroke patients?
claim_mapping: PES before extubation provides distinct exploratory ICU treatment evidence alongside postextubation studies.
caveat: 32 prospective treated patients versus 32 historical matched controls; nonrandomized, pneumonia difference nonsignificant; not the n60 randomized trial.

title: Dysphagia after stroke: research advances in treatment interventions.
claim_mapping: Contemporary stroke dysphagia treatment framework distinguishes protective care from swallowing rehabilitation.
caveat: Review; numerical effects must come from primary trials; does not establish national underuse from coded rates.

title: Validation of the DIGEST-FEES as a Global Outcome Measure for Pharyngeal Dysphagia in Parkinson's Disease.
claim_mapping: Disease-specific FEES severity measurement validation in Parkinson disease is adjacent, but not directly applicable to aggregate R13.
caveat: 66 PD FEES videos; not validated for the present all-neurological or stroke administrative cohort.

title: Pharyngeal electrical stimulation for postextubation dysphagia in acute stroke: a randomized controlled pilot trial.
claim_mapping: Original randomized PES postextubation pilot provides the primary trial report behind subsequent recovery/economic analyses.
caveat: n60 severe dysphagic stroke patients; primary reintubation endpoint 13% vs33%, p=.067, did not reach significance; favorable secondary endpoints are exploratory.

title: The assessment of dysphagia after stroke: state of the art and future directions.
claim_mapping: Contemporary assessment hierarchy and indications for instrumental evaluation; supports interpretation of coded dysphagia/FEES.
caveat: State-of-the-art review, not a claim that every R13-coded episode needs FEES.

title: Bilateral vocal cord palsy as complication of CNS tuberculosis.
claim_mapping: Rare tuberculosis-related vocal-cord palsy case is mechanistically adjacent to tracheostomy but unnecessary for broad early-rehabilitation burden.
caveat: Single case; cannot support prevalence or outcome estimates.

title: Sarcopenic Dysphagia Revisited: A Cross-Sectional Study in Hospitalized Geriatric Patients.
claim_mapping: Useful only to qualify a proposed sarcopenic explanation of dysphagia; current manuscripts should avoid inferring mechanisms from malnutrition codes.
caveat: Selected n109 geriatrics cohort; no significant dysphagia-sarcopenia association; not proof that sarcopenic dysphagia cannot occur.

title: [Erratum to: Diagnostics and treatment of post-stroke dysphagia].
claim_mapping: Erratum linked to PMID37160432; bibliographic housekeeping if that review is cited.
caveat: No abstract; not independent evidence and correction content requires full-text checking before using corrected details.

title: [Diagnostics and treatment of post-stroke dysphagia].
claim_mapping: German clinical management context specifically for post-stroke screening, indicated FEES and care.
caveat: Narrative review overlapping English Lancet assessment/treatment reviews; cite once for German clinical context, not repeatedly for the same claim. Linked erratum PMID37318543.

title: Costs of post-stroke dysphagia during acute hospitalization from a health-insurance perspective.
claim_mapping: Direct German FEES-based acute-stroke expenditure study anchors resource-burden discussion.
caveat: n674 FEES-selected patients; severe FEDSS6 associated with modeled insurer expenditure; reimbursement is not actual cost, and observational association does not establish savings.

title: Relationship between post-stroke dysphagia and pharyngeal sensory impairment.
claim_mapping: Sensory and secretion-management deficits demonstrate clinically relevant heterogeneity concealed by R13 coding.
caveat: Prospective acute-stroke n57; association with clinical severity, not causal outcomes or treatment benefit.

title: Dysphagia for medication in Parkinson's disease.
claim_mapping: Medication-swallowing impairment in Parkinson disease illustrates a separate phenotype not measured here.
caveat: n66 PD patients, medication-specific assessment; no current manuscript endpoint or subgroup requiring citation.

title: Clinical determinants and neural correlates of presbyphagia in community-dwelling older adults.
claim_mapping: Age-related swallowing reserve may contextualize age gradients but cannot explain them causally.
caveat: 64 community-dwelling older adults; presbyphagic alterations are not equivalent to inpatient coded dysphagia.

title: Detecting myositis as a cause of unexplained dysphagia: Proposal for a diagnostic algorithm.
claim_mapping: Myositis differential-diagnosis algorithm supports treatable etiology, but current paper does not study unexplained dysphagia diagnosis.
caveat: Selected 72 patients with IIM-compatible pattern; narrow diagnostic cohort, not early-rehabilitation prevalence.

title: Oropharyngeal Dysphagia and Impaired Motility of the Upper Gastrointestinal Tract-Is There a Clinical Link in Neurocritical Care?
claim_mapping: Neurocritical gastric dysmotility and swallowing dysfunction may share severity-related factors, outside measured endpoint set.
caveat: n976 neurologic ICU patients; high gastric residual volume is not captured by R13/PEG and is not investigated in these manuscripts.

title: Comparison of Simultaneous Swallowing Endoscopy and Videofluoroscopy in Neurogenic Dysphagia.
claim_mapping: Direct simultaneous FEES/VFSS comparison supports complementary instrumental assessment and cautions against inferring all assessment from one procedure code.
caveat: Prospective n49; modality comparison, not national service utilization or intervention efficacy.

title: Detecting myasthenia gravis as a cause of unclear dysphagia with an endoscopic tensilon test.
claim_mapping: Endoscopic tensilon test for myasthenia diagnosis is relevant to disease-specific evaluation, not the burden analysis.
caveat: Selected n100 unclear dysphagia cohort; no tested InEK subgroup requiring its diagnostic-accuracy estimate.

title: Standardized Endoscopic Swallowing Evaluation for Tracheostomy Decannulation in Critically Ill Neurologic Patients - a prospective evaluation.
claim_mapping: Prospective SESETD decannulation pathway directly relevant to dysphagia-tracheostomy care in early rehabilitation.
caveat: n377 neurologic ICU patients after mechanical-ventilation weaning; not a national early-rehab cohort and not causal evidence from tracheostomy codes.

title: Predictors, outcome and characteristics of oropharyngeal dysphagia in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy.
claim_mapping: IIM dysphagia severity and pneumonia illustrate non-stroke heterogeneity but are outside current disease-specific analyses.
caveat: Retrospective n71 IIM patients; general neurogenic classification reference suffices for mixed-etiology limitation.

title: Expiratory Muscle Strength Training for Therapy of Pharyngeal Dysphagia in Parkinson's Disease.
claim_mapping: PD-specific randomized expiratory-muscle training evidence is relevant to a disease-specific treatment review, not current main results.
caveat: n50 PD patients; cannot generalize to severe mixed early-rehabilitation cohort or claim general reduced pneumonia.

title: Dysphagia in Patients With Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019-Potential Neurologic Etiologies.
claim_mapping: Severe COVID-related dysphagia case series is adjacent to critical-illness rehabilitation, but no COVID-specific question is analyzed.
caveat: Six selected tracheotomized patients; no general burden or causal efficacy estimate.

title: Effect of Capsaicinoids on Neurophysiological, Biochemical, and Mechanical Parameters of Swallowing Function.
claim_mapping: Capsaicinoid physiology in healthy individuals is outside clinical burden study scope.
caveat: Healthy-subject mechanistic experiment; not patient outcome evidence.

title: Dysphagia in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody disease as a surrogate of brain involvement?
claim_mapping: Rare NMOSD/MOGAD-related dysphagia illustrates broad etiology, but not needed without such subgroup analysis.
caveat: n13 selected patients; cannot estimate dysphagia burden in broad neurological rehabilitation.

title: Inter-rater and test-retest reliability of the "standardized endoscopic swallowing evaluation for tracheostomy decannulation in critically ill neurologic patients".
claim_mapping: Reliability of standardized secretion/swallow/cough assessment underpins FEES-based decannulation pathways.
caveat: Small video-rating reliability study; not comparative care effectiveness. Complement to prospective SESETD study rather than independent clinical replication.

title: Neurogenic Dysphagia: Systematic Review and Proposal of a Classification System.
claim_mapping: Validated phenotypic heterogeneity explains why binary R13 coding cannot substitute for clinical dysphagia characterization.
caveat: Systematic review plus 1,012-video validation; clinical FEES phenotypes do not validate an administrative severity scale.

title: Effects of cognitive and motor dual-tasks on oropharyngeal swallowing assessed with FEES in healthy individuals.
claim_mapping: Healthy young-adult dual-task swallowing experiment does not support current hospital burden claims.
caveat: n27 healthy participants; no patient outcomes.

title: Bilateral Vocal Fold Paralysis in Myasthenia Gravis: A Case Report and Literature Review.
claim_mapping: Rare myasthenia-related vocal-fold paralysis case illustrates a reversible diagnosis, unnecessary for aggregate outcomes.
caveat: Case report/review; not representative of the care cohort.

title: Effect of cognitive and motor dual-task on oropharyngeal swallowing in Parkinson's disease.
claim_mapping: PD dual-task swallowing illustrates attention effects but not a measured administrative exposure or outcome.
caveat: n30 PD patients; physiologic task comparison, not inpatient resource study.

title: Targeting the sensory feedback within the swallowing network-Reversing artificially induced pharyngolaryngeal hypesthesia by central and peripheral stimulation strategies.
claim_mapping: Artificial sensory-lesion neurostimulation physiology in healthy volunteers is outside current clinical burden scope.
caveat: n10 healthy volunteers; experimental hypesthesia not equivalent to stroke or early rehabilitation.

title: Predictors of Pharyngeal Dysphagia in Patients with Parkinson's Disease.
claim_mapping: PD-specific dysphagia predictors are not needed without a PD subgroup hypothesis.
caveat: n200 PD patients; thresholds cannot be transferred to all neurological early-rehabilitation admissions.

title: The Impact of Dysphagia in Myositis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
claim_mapping: Myositis systematic review addresses disease-specific prevalence and treatment, outside current principal questions.
caveat: Pooled IIM prevalence not comparable with either InEK OPS cohort; broad phenotype reference already covers etiologic diversity.

title: Oropharyngeal freezing and its relation to dysphagia - An analogy to freezing of gait.
claim_mapping: Oropharyngeal freezing is a Parkinson-specific phenotype; stroke comparison exists but not an inpatient outcome study.
caveat: n50 PD plus retrospective stroke/healthy control videos; not prevalence evidence for the present cohorts.

title: Effect of Intestinal Levodopa-Carbidopa Infusion on Pharyngeal Dysphagia: Results from a Retrospective Pilot Study in Patients with Parkinson's Disease.
claim_mapping: LCIG in PD is a highly specific treatment pilot not needed for broad resource burden.
caveat: Only11 pre/post FEES cases; overall score change nonsignificant. PubMed abstract has a duplicated/truncated Results string, so no secondary numerical claims used.

title: FEES-based assessment of pharyngeal hypesthesia-Proposal and validation of a new test procedure.
claim_mapping: Original FEES sensory-test validation supports detailed methods only if the technique itself is discussed.
caveat: 20 healthy volunteers before/after anesthesia; current manuscripts do not perform this sensory test. Clinical application paper PMID36793109 more relevant.

title: Dysphagia as Isolated Manifestation of Jo-1 Associated Myositis?
claim_mapping: Isolated Jo-1 myositis dysphagia case is differential-diagnosis context but not useful for current aggregate claims.
caveat: Single case; no general outcome estimate.

title: Extubation Readiness in Critically Ill Stroke Patients.
claim_mapping: Clinical dysphagia severity and extubation failure provide direct airway/resource-burden context in severe stroke.
caveat: Prospective n133; FEDSS associated with extubation failure, observational; DEFISS development not full external validation.

title: Predicting Dysphagia with National Institute of Health Stroke Scale: Distinction between Infra- and Supratentorial Region is Essential.
claim_mapping: Stroke severity and lesion location alter dysphagia risk, emphasizing unmeasured confounding and the limits of R13 coding.
caveat: Retrospective FEES-selected n687; NIHSS has moderate accuracy and is an adjunct, not replacement, for swallowing assessment.
